what_was_built: A durable operator command channel and durable sync progress. edged writes a command row; the pmsd worker that owns the socket claims it under its own runtime_generation CAS and raises the DR through the existing serialized writer. Nothing outside pmsd emits a frame. The DS->DE staging, the atomic PublishResyncGeneration barrier, the generation ownership guard and the automatic initial sync are reused unchanged.
safety_model: The claim is one UPDATE whose WHERE clause carries every rule: runtime_generation matches (this worker still owns the interface), resync_command_generation matches (the command was issued to THIS worker, not one it replaced), and sync_status is not RESYNC_IN_PROGRESS (no second staging window). Zero rows means 'nothing to do' for all three, which is the correct response to each. A duplicate click cannot produce a second DR because the row can only be consumed once.
mirror_safety: The last known-good mirror is never cleared at resync start. Records are staged under a new generation and become live only at the atomic publish; an interrupted sync therefore leaves the previous guest list serving, which the UI states plainly rather than leaving the operator to guess.
no_invented_numbers: FIAS provides no record total before DE. There is deliberately no total, percentage or remaining-count column, field or UI element; the schema, the API type and a UI test all enforce the absence. What is shown is the real staged count and a sentence explaining why that is all there is.
